findings.title: QosPanel.open's null guard is dead-on-arrival — typed Dictionary from pipes.get throws before the guard (the r2-B1 pattern, proven to throw)

findings.recommended_fix: Untype the local (var p = sim.pipes.get(pipe_id)) or pipes.get(pipe_id, {}); audit the same pattern repo-wide.

findings.title: 'Strands re-thicken on QoS apply' (spec clause) has no automated pin — alloc->view rebuild unasserted; a constant thickness passes the suite

findings.recommended_fix: Pin: apply set_lanes to a live arc, assert rebuilt shares differ per lane (pipe_arc._shares mirror).

findings.title: Class-cycle button is a provable no-op on the single-lane rung (order size 1 -> same lane)
findings.evidence:
var cur: int = order.find(int(_cls_lane[cls]))
_cls_lane[cls] = order[(cur + 1) % order.size()]
findings.detail: On rung 1 (Standard only) the cycle re-selects the same lane; enabled button does nothing. Cosmetic UX.
findings.recommended_fix: Disable the cycle button when order.size() == 1, or hide it on rung 1.

findings.title: Radius-8 geometry + lane speeds make the longest arcs breach email's 2000ms tolerance with zero congestion
findings.evidence: LANE_SPEED_MILLI [200,100,60] + latency_tol_ms 2000 vs longest-arc milli lengths; _latency_breach_long_pipe relies on it.
findings.detail: Latency latch on long arcs is transit-time-driven, not congestion-driven. Gentle default network stays clean (pinned); balance observation for the GDD's Numerical Design review.
findings.recommended_fix: Note in the GDD, or tune tolerance/arc lengths if long-haul email should survive quiet transit.

findings.title: _cmd_set_lanes accepts alloc totals below 100, silently stranding capacity (only > 100 is rejected)
